q2_loopback_4318.answer: No, not with today's mechanism. In ref/claude-shell.mjs, shellProfile()'s loopbackDenied path allows network-bind/inbound/outbound on localhost:* broadly, then appends per-port DENY rules only for ports already listening on the host at job start (scanListeningPorts via lsof), excluding proxyPort. That is a blocklist of pre-existing listeners, not an allowlist of one port; no rule shape grants only 4318. validateNetworkAllow() also refuses any non-empty networkAllow outright ('not yet supported'); the only non-loopback allow is the fixed api.anthropic.com:443 CONNECT proxy. REPORT ONLY, no changes made.
q2_loopback_4318.evidence: node net.createServer().listen(4318,'127.0.0.1') then net.connect(4318,...): {"port":4318,"listen":"ok","connect":"ok"}. Same probe on port 4319 (arbitrary other port): {"port":4319,"listen":"ok","connect":"ok"}. net.connect(80,'93.184.216.34') (external IP): 'error: EPERM'. So this sandbox is loopback-open (minus pre-existing listeners) or closed to the outside world, never narrowed to a single port.
